entries.rationale: Keep abandonment as a configurable pathway policy only when enabled by the selected profile; the E1 plan explicitly makes it optional and requires a terminal reason and censoring fields. The conditional probability shape is suitable if denominators and conditioning are explicit.

The catalogue may retain this input, but the generic MVP contract does not require an assisted-mobility behavior model. Keep it out of MVP profile fixtures until an in-scope pathway requires it and its effect on resources or routes is specified.

A generic routing-compliance probability would add a patient decision rule without a defined route-choice or compliance mechanism in the MVP contract. Preserve the ID as deferred; enable only with a scoped route policy and explicit conditioned denominators.
No generic MVP behavior or resource effect for companions is specified. The proposed future consumer and deferred profile stage are appropriate; revisit only if relevance is established.

The name and proposed use risk injecting external admission arrivals in addition to patients whose admission disposition is generated by the ED pathway. Define this as pathway-generated admission requests or an explicitly external fixture input, never both; distinguish that demand from receiving-bed offers.
entries.replacement: Use `hospital_boundary.admission_requests` for ED-generated requests and document external fixture demand as mutually exclusive input mode; do not treat general hospital admission counts as ED arrivals.

entries.rationale: The generic structured unit contract is too vague for the minimum admission boundary. The E0 plan requires finite, destination-compatible ED-eligible offers with lifetime/withdrawal and competing-demand assumptions. Model offer records explicitly; do not infer available ED beds from raw inpatient counts.
entries.replacement: Retain the stable ID/key but define a finite ED-eligible bed-offer schedule with destination compatibility, availability interval/expiry, withdrawal, and explicit competing-demand assumptions; numeric leaves carry units.

entries.rationale: Keep transfer/transport as a boundary record for enabled transfer pathways. The E0 plan distinguishes ambulance arrival, triage, handover, offload, and crew-release clocks; those events must not be collapsed into one elapsed duration.

A structured boundary input is appropriate for explicitly modeled diagnostic dependencies. Require named dependency/resource and explicit timing/capacity units at numeric leaves; do not imply a whole-hospital diagnostic model.
Whole-hospital mechanisms are outside the generic ED MVP and the parameter spec explicitly excludes a detailed whole-hospital model. Keep the ID deferred with no current E0 consumer.
Fatigue has no MVP consumer or defined state/update mechanism. The spec directs optional complexity to remain deferred until evidence and decision relevance justify activation.
Learning has no MVP consumer or defined state/update mechanism. Keep it deferred until evidence and a decision-relevant behavior contract exist.
Crowding feedback is an extension requiring scoped acceptance and an explicit mechanism; the generic MVP requires occupancy reporting but does not require crowding to alter behavior.
Detailed physiology is explicitly optional and has no generic MVP consumer. Preserve as deferred; do not turn it into an implicit deterioration or clinical policy.

An explicit initial-state input is needed to describe occupancy and ongoing work without hidden defaults. Require internally consistent entity, resource, and event state; an empty deterministic initialization remains a valid MVP fixture.

Retain as optional initialization detail for in-progress work. Values must be non-negative durations interpreted from the run clock origin and must not be counted again as service already completed; not required in the one-patient fresh-start fixture.

Warm-up is appropriately staged for hardened experiments rather than the functional MVP. Keep it an explicit experiment setting when introduced, with reported metric windows excluding warm-up as declared.

cross_cutting_issues.issue: Admission demand may duplicate admission requests generated by the ED pathway.
cross_cutting_issues.recommendation: Clarify pathway-generated requests versus external fixture demand and keep them mutually exclusive; model receiving capacity as separate finite, compatible, time-bounded bed offers.

cross_cutting_issues.issue: MVP seed stage is inconsistent with the delivery contract.
cross_cutting_issues.recommendation: Promote the single run seed and repeatability input to MVP_candidate; leave multi-stream derivation and exact width to Kairos 01.

cross_cutting_issues.issue: A runtime global time-unit switch conflicts with canonical seconds and per-field unit-bearing values.
cross_cutting_issues.recommendation: Carry source units on each time field, normalize durations to seconds at input, then convert once to ticks after C0 resolves tick resolution, origin, precision, and rounding. No numeric tick resolution is recommended here.

cross_cutting_issues.issue: Timestamped schedules and observed timestamps need an explicit conversion contract.
cross_cutting_issues.recommendation: C0 still needs to decide origin, timezone/DST handling, precision, rounding, and recording-delay semantics; E0 should reject ambiguous or unrepresentable inputs.

cross_cutting_issues.issue: Measurement mappings can be mistaken for generative inputs.
cross_cutting_issues.recommendation: Keep elapsed/queue observations, event definitions, cohort criteria, metric denominators, missingness, and censoring in the observation/calibration boundary; do not feed observed elapsed intervals into service distributions without reviewed transformation.

cross_cutting_issues.issue: Structured contracts have no single scalar unit.
cross_cutting_issues.recommendation: Require explicit typed units on every numeric leaf and version categorical coding; structural matrix coverage does not settle consumer semantics.
